title: Coefficient parameters and normalization predicates for locally closed extension
statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$ [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] with an arbitrary commutative ring sheaf $R$ on its pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], bundle these parameters as LocallyClosedCoefficients. A coefficient immersion $a:S\to X$ is an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion] and an isomorphism $a^{-1}R\cong R_S$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Its identity and composition use the canonical ring inverse-image identity and composition maps [def-weil-pbc-strict-tower-operations]. Its pull and push are actual tensor pullback and direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; pullComp is the specified normalized inverse-image composition comparison. This records and relocates the existing parameter definitions, without changing any of them. Also name the following formulas for arbitrary categories and functors, to be specialized to these module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Given F:C→D, L:D→C, r:FL≅1 and adj:F⊣L, open normalization means adj.unit_M followed by r_M is 1_M. Given P:C→D, d:PL→1 and e:F≅P, closed normalization means r_M=L(e_M) followed by d_M. Given H:C→D, r:HL≅1, A∈D, M∈C, t:L(A)→M and e:A≅H(M), object normalization means L(e) followed by r_M equals t. Finally for Ea:B→C, Eb:A→B, La:C→B, Lb:B→A, Lab:C→A, H:A→C, ra:EaLa≅1, rb:EbLb≅1, rh:HLab≅1, c:Lab≅LaLb and e:EbEa≅H, binary normalization means, for every M, Lab(e_M) followed by rh_M equals c_(Ea(Eb(M))) followed by Lb(ra_(Eb(M))) followed by rb_M. These are transparent names for the original equations, with composite-functor object types definitionally simplified. LocallyClosedCompositeRestrictionMap is the explicitly constructed right-hand-side morphism in the binary equation, named over these arbitrary categories before specialization; it is exactly the displayed threefold composite.
